messages.subject: Looking to hire R developers
messages.body_plain:
Hello members of "The sweetest R-help group this side of the Mississippi"

My company is looking to hire R developers. If you are inetersted and/or know others who are interested, please have the send tehir resumes to recru...@biganalytixs.com. Any relevant experience with utilities and energy space, please have it highlighted the resume

The following is the profile we are looking for.

Your Mission:
Design and develop modular, well-tested, well-documented, reusable, and extensible R code for a novel clinical trial statistical application.
Peer review R code and provide critical, constructive feedback.
Design and implement statistical tests to validate the application.
Work with product managers to craft feature requirements, question assumptions, assess feasibility, and estimate cost/benefit tradeoffs.
Work with other engineers to create data contracts of all integration points. Question assumptions and assess cost/benefit to arrive at the best solution.
Ability to work independently on complex and diverse issues and propose solutions

Your Competencies:
Proficiency in R programming, including extensive hands-on experiences in the following technologies:
RStudio
Shiny
tidyverse
devtools
R6
Sparklyr
Proficiency in SQL programming
Exposure to statistical modeling and analysis. Familiarity with concepts of supervised and unsupervised machine learning models.
Familiarity using github and Git version control
Familiarity with Azure technologies such as hdinsight clusters (spark, hive, Hadoop, ranger etc).
Strong verbal and written communication

Your Education & Experience:
Masters or Post Graduate in computer science, statistics, operations research, or data science or in a related field with decent foundation in statistical methodology
4 plus years of experience in R programming and statistical analysis

messages.subject: #maptimeDavis & D-RUG: Earth Engine & R for presentation-quality contextual maps
messages.subject_clean: #maptimeDavis & D-RUG: Earth Engine & R for presentation-quality contextual maps
messages.body_plain:
#MAPTIMEDAVIS & DAVIS R USERS GROUP WORKSHOP: EARTH ENGINE & R FOR PRESENTATION-QUALITY CONTEXTUAL MAPS

Description: We will combine the power of Earth Engine with the user-friendliness of R to generate beautiful, presentation-quality contextual maps. The workshop will focus on Landsat imagery, but is generalizable to other remote sensing products. Creativity is encouraged! We will use Earth Engine to access, filter, and crop data for download, and then use R to wrangle our dataset and generate beautiful, high-resolution plots.

Location: Online via Zoom. Please register for the link to participate.

Registration: Register Here <https://registration.genomecenter.ucdavis.edu/events/MaptimeDavisWorkshopEarth/>

Cost: Free of charge

Learning Objectives: Attendees will learn how to access, filter, and download data using Google Earth Engine, and to process and plot raster datasets using a tidyverse approach in R.

Prerequisites: No experience necessary, but Earth Engine and R exposure are a bonus!

Software: Attendees will need to have a Google Earth Engine account prior to attending the workshop (may take a few days to process a request for a new account), and have R installed. Attendees will also need to have the following R packages installed: tidyverse, raster, sf, rgdal, RStoolbox.

Presenter: Christian John

Presenter Bio: Christian is a 4th-year PhD student in the Graduate Group in Ecology using novel remote sensing data to explore how snowmelt and plant growth drive bighorn sheep migration.

Whenever possible, #maptimeDavis Workshops will be recorded and posted on the DataLab YouTube channel <https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCTooXK1RiSHNbWsmeqz0W6g>. #maptimeDavis Studio will not be recorded to encourage open discussion. Weekly reminders will be sent on the Geospatial Email List <https://lists.ucdavis.edu/sympa/info/geospatial>.

#maptimeDavis Workshops and Studio are a product of UC Davis DataLab’s Spatial Sciences Research Cluster <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/spatial-sciences/> and are supported by the contributions and participation of our community. Please send questions to Michele Tobias mmto...@ucdavis.edu
